nodes.title: Alignment score is the negated linear-penalty cost

nodes.summary: The cost of one alignment column.
nodes.title: Cost of an alignment column under linear gap penalties

nodes.summary: The cost of an alignment: the sum of its column costs.
nodes.title: Cost of an alignment under linear gap penalties

nodes.summary: The end cell is reached by some score `s' ≤ s` iff `s` is at least the optimal Needleman–Wunsch cost.
nodes.title: The wavefront algorithm computes the optimal alignment cost

nodes.summary: The wavefront algorithm is exact: the end cell is reached by some score `s' ≤ s` iff some alignment of `xs` and `ys` costs at most `s`. Hence the least such `s` is the optimal cost.
nodes.title: Exactness of the wavefront alignment algorithm

nodes.summary: Follow matching letters along diagonal `k` from offset `h`, with fuel.
nodes.title: Fuelled extension of matches along a diagonal

nodes.summary: Linear gap penalties: match `0`, mismatch `mismatch ≥ 1`, each gap column `gap ≥ 1`.
nodes.title: Linear gap penalties

nodes.summary: The largest valid offset on diagonal `k`: `h ≤ |ys|` and `v = h - k ≤ |xs|`.
nodes.title: Largest valid offset on a diagonal

nodes.summary: The substitution score in the maximization convention of `nwScore`: `0` for a match and `-mismatch` for a mismatch (the gap score is `-gap`).
nodes.title: Substitution score from linear gap penalties

nodes.summary: The match extension ("slide") along diagonal `k` from offset `h`.
nodes.title: Match extension (slide) along a diagonal

nodes.summary: The wavefront recurrence with fuel (fuel `s + 1` suffices; see `wavefront`). `none` stands for an unreachable diagonal. Offsets proposed by an operation are clamped to the largest valid offset of the target diagonal before sliding.
nodes.title: Fuelled wavefront recurrence

nodes.summary: Completeness: every alignment of a pair of prefixes is dominated on its diagonal by the wavefront of its exact cost.
nodes.title: Completeness of the wavefront algorithm

nodes.summary: Soundness: a wavefront offset is a valid cell of its diagonal, reachable by an alignment of the corresponding prefixes with cost at most `s`.
nodes.title: Soundness of the wavefront algorithm

nodes.summary: The furthest-reaching offset of score `s` on diagonal `k = h - v`.
nodes.title: Furthest-reaching wavefront offset

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
